title: Priced for Perfection
briefing: Nimbus Cloud trades at about 60 times earnings; Harborline Shipping at about 8. Both report on day 15. Which one has more to lose from a small disappointment?
objective: High-P/E growth stocks carry high expectations; a small miss can hit them hard.
debrief: Both companies came in slightly below estimates on day 15. Nimbus Cloud, priced for fast growth at a P/E near 60, gapped down and kept sliding as buyers rethought the growth story. Harborline, already cheap at a P/E near 8, barely moved and later raised its dividend on day 22. A disciplined player kept the expensive stock small going into the report and let the cheap, steady one do the work.

assets.name: Nimbus Cloud
assets.blurb: Rents cloud servers to businesses. Shares trade at about 60 times earnings.

assets.name: Harborline Shipping
assets.blurb: Moves containers between major ports. Shares trade at about 8 times earnings.

news.headline: Nimbus Cloud and Harborline Shipping both report on day 15
news.body: Analysts expect Nimbus Cloud sales to grow 30% and Harborline profit to stay flat.

news.headline: Nimbus Cloud sales grow 28%, just short of the 30% expected
news.body: Growth is still fast, but slower than the shares had assumed.

news.headline: Harborline profit comes in slightly below estimates
news.body: Shipping volumes were steady; fuel costs were a little higher than expected.

news.headline: Harborline raises its dividend by 10%
news.body: The company says its cash flow can support a higher payout.

basic.text: Keep Nimbus Cloud under 20% of your portfolio going into its day-15 report
Hold Harborline Shipping at the end
